Ahead of your contract anniversary next quarter I pulled a short snapshot of your Q3 usage and some hour-of-day heatmaps to check whether your Dedicated fleet sizing still matches production realities. I attached a small excerpt (atlas_q3_usage_excerpt.csv) that highlights the sustained tail of inference traffic tied to your new "smart-summarize" release.

Quick ask: can we schedule a 30-min sync this week to run through three quick scenarios (conservative, balanced, growth) and agree next steps? My thinking:
- Validate current steady-state utilization and tail spikes
- Decide runway buffer (10% vs 25% vs 40%) before the renewal
- Propose a short amendment (if needed) with a 60-day early-burst tranche and firmer SLA windows

I can bring a recommended sizing checklist and cost deltas. Attaching the usage excerpt and a sample internal load dump you can share if helpful.

Thanks,

- Avoid any user-visible throttles during Dec 10–20 marketing window
- Keep amendment friction low (one-line DocuSign amendment preferred)
- Provide 3 options: Minimal buffer (10% headroom), Safety buffer (25%), Growth buffer (40% + short 60-day burst pool)

Please include: estimated additional GPUs, expected monthly delta, impact to our SLA exposure, and a recommended fallback (model variant or burst routing) if capacity bumps. Attach the scenario_summary.pdf and a short exec note I can send to Marc.

Team — attached is the scenario_summary.pdf with three recommended options and quick bullets below. High-level: Atlas's 2.6x peak uplift + KV cache pressure suggests their working set is driving inefficient KG cache hits. We recommend a combined approach: small capacity add + short burst tranche + routing policy.

Options (short):
1) Minimal buffer (Conservative)
   - +8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (adds ~12% steady capacity)
   - Estimated delta: +$28k/mo
   - SLA exposure: low; relies on existing routing; no burst pool

2) Safety buffer (Balanced) — recommended
   - +15 x A100-equivalent GPUs (adds ~25% steady capacity)
   - Estimated delta: +$52k/mo
   - SLA exposure: minimal; includes 60-day 30 GPU burst tranche for holiday window

3) Growth buffer (Aggressive)
   - +24 x A100-equivalent GPUs (adds ~40% steady capacity)
   - Estimated delta: +$92k/mo
   - SLA exposure: lowest; includes automatic fallback to smaller model variant under extreme tail and permanent larger commit

Risks & mitigations:
- If KV cache churn continues, steady GPUs will underperform; mitigation = prefix caching + model quantization recommendation (low-latency mode) we can apply non-disruptively.
- Quick amendment required for balanced option: 2–3 business days to DocuSign, 7–10 days operational lead to provision burst pool in Dedicated.

I attached a one-page exec blurb you can send to Marc (exec_note.txt embedded in scenario_summary.pdf).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: scenario_summary.pdf

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-27T15:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: GPU runway rebalance — planning checklist and risk window

Marc — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the load dump. Ben and Neha reviewed and recommend the Safety buffer (option 2) as the balance of cost and risk. Summary and next steps below: 

Summary recommendation (Balanced) — Safety buffer:
- Add 15 A100-equivalent GPUs to steady Dedicated pool (est. +25% capacity)
- Provision a 60-day 30-GPU burst tranche for Dec 8–Jan 8 to cover the holiday campaign
- Include automatic fallback routing to a quantized model variant for extreme tail beyond burst pool

Operational timeline and minimal amendment:
1) Redwood prepares a single-line DocuSign amendment with the 60-day burst clause and the monthly delta (attached: proposed_amendment.docx). We can have that to you within 24 hours.
2) Upon signature, provisioning lead time: 7 business days for steady add; 3 business days to enable burst routing after provisioning window is open.
3) Pre-holiday runbook: we will run a mocked peak test (3-hour window) with Atlas EngOps on Dec 3 to validate routes and cache settings.

Action items for Atlas:
- Confirm approval to proceed with the Balanced option by 2026-12-03 EOD to meet Dec 10 readiness.
- Sign the DocuSign amendment once received.
- Provide a single contact for the Dec 3 runbook (name + pager).

If you want to tighten cost, we can convert some of the steady add to a longer burst runway instead — happy to discuss tradeoffs.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(e) evelyn.hart@redwood.ai | (m) +1-415-555-0142

Attachments: proposed_amendment.docx
